Name: CLR Memory Management, Zero-Allocation & Performance Suite
DefaultSystemPrompt:
You are a Principal High-Performance .NET Architect expert in CLR internals, Garbage Collector mechanics (Gen 0/1/2, LOH, POH), memory allocation profiling, and zero-allocation techniques (Span<T>, Memory<T>, ArrayPool<T>, System.IO.Pipelines).
1. Provide optimized, low-allocation C# solutions.
2. Address boxing/unboxing, closure captures, and Stack vs. Heap allocation trade-offs explicitly.
CRITICAL: Keep your internal reasoning under 200 tokens. Do not explore multiple alternatives. Think concisely and output the solution immediately.
DefaultUserPromptSuffix:
MANDATORY OUTPUT CONSTRAINTS:
1. Wrap code in ```csharp ... ``` blocks.
2. Detail the exact GC generation impact (Gen 0/1/2 or LOH) and heap allocation profile in explanations.
3. Do not explain background theory. Plan your steps in no more than 3 bullet points inside thinking tags, then output the code directly.
DefaultJudgeSystemPrompt:
You are a strict technical evaluation judge for .NET Memory Management and Performance Optimization.

CRITICAL EVALUATION GUIDELINES:
1. Memory & Span Semantics:
   - Verify that 'ref struct' (Span<T>) is not captured across await boundaries or inside heap-allocated closures.
   - Ensure 'ArrayPool<T>.Shared.Return' is enclosed in a try/finally block.
   - Verify that string parsing uses 'ReadOnlySpan<char>' with manual slicing (IndexOf/Slice) without allocating intermediate string arrays.
2. BCL & Pipelines:
   - Verify 'System.IO.Pipelines' cursor advancement using 'Reader.AdvanceTo()'.
   - Acknowledge 'FrozenDictionary' layout benefits for immutable lookups.
3. Output Formatting:
   - Output your decision on the very first line as:
   VERDICT: PASS
   or
   VERDICT: FAIL

   Followed by a brief one-sentence reason.

Tests.Name: Trap: Span<T> Across Await Boundary

Criteria.Description: Explains that 'ref struct' types reside strictly on the Stack and the compiler forbids their use across await in async methods because state machines are allocated on the Heap
Provides a valid refactoring that compiles in C# (using synchronous helper methods or ReadOnlyMemory<char>)

Tests.Name: Memory: LOH Pressure from Temporary Arrays (ArrayPool)

Criteria.Description: Explains that objects larger than 85,000 bytes are allocated on the Large Object Heap (LOH), increasing fragmentation and triggering costly Gen 2 collections
Implements ArrayPool<byte>.Shared.Rent() and ensures buffer return with Return() inside a try/finally block

Tests.Name: Memory: RecyclableMemoryStream vs MemoryStream for High Throughput

Criteria.Description: Explains that MemoryStream allocates a buffer on each use and ToArray() duplicates memory, increasing GC pressure in high-frequency operations
Refactors using RecyclableMemoryStreamManager.GetStream() to obtain streams from a reusable pool, eliminating repetitive allocations

Tests.Name: Stack Allocation (stackalloc) vs Heap

Criteria.Description: Declares and initializes the temporary buffer using 'stackalloc' to allocate memory on the Stack
Manipulates the Stack buffer via Span<byte> without requiring direct 'unsafe' code blocks

Tests.Name: Memory Leaks via Event Subscription

Criteria.Description: Explains that the Singleton publisher holds a Strong Reference to the PriceDisplay instance, preventing its collection by the Garbage Collector
Implements the IDisposable interface to unsubscribe from the event (-=) or uses the WeakEventManager / WeakReference pattern

Tests.Name: Memory Optimization with Span<T>

Criteria.Description: Uses ReadOnlySpan<char> or AsSpan()
Completely eliminates .Split() usage by applying manual slicing with IndexOf / Slice
Explicitly mentions the reduction of Garbage Collector (GC) pressure

Tests.Name: Performance: Closure Allocations in Lambdas

Criteria.Description: Explains that capturing local variables forces the creation of a closure class instance (DisplayClass) on the Heap on each execution
Refactors the code avoiding Heap allocations through static lambdas or a direct imperative loop

Tests.Name: Performance: FrozenDictionary<TKey, TValue> for Read-Only Data (.NET 8+)

Criteria.Description: Explains that FrozenDictionary optimizes internal layout for frequent reads with perfect or near-perfect hashing, outperforming Dictionary for immutable read-only collections
Refactors the static field using FrozenDictionary<string, string> initialized with .ToFrozenDictionary() during application startup

Tests.Name: Performance: Multiple Re-evaluation of IEnumerable

Criteria.Description: Explains that deferred execution causes the LINQ query pipeline to re-execute from scratch on each invocation (.Any(), .Count(), foreach)
Refactors the logic materializing the collection only once (e.g., ToArray/ToList) or restructuring the flow into a single iteration

Tests.Name: Performance: Stream Parsing with System.IO.Pipelines

Criteria.Description: Explains that System.IO.Pipelines automatically manages buffer memory (ReadOnlySequence), eliminating copying and Heap allocations
Implements PipeReader.ReadAsync(), processes ReadOnlySequence<byte>, and frees consumed memory with Reader.AdvanceTo()

Tests.Name: Performance: Value Type Boxing and Unboxing

Criteria.Description: Explains that Boxing allocates memory on the Heap to wrap a value type (struct) inside a reference object (object), increasing GC pressure
Eliminates Boxing by refactoring to generics (T) and direct interpolation or ISpanFormattable

Tests.Name: Performance: ValueTask vs Task for Hot Paths

Criteria.Description: Explains that Task<T> always allocates an object on the Heap even on synchronous completions, whereas ValueTask<T> avoids this allocation on the happy path
Refactors the method returning ValueTask<string?> and directly returning the cached value on the synchronous path without creating a Task object

Tests.Name: String Concatenation and Heap Pressure

Criteria.Description: Explicitly explains System.String immutability and excessive Heap allocations in loops
Replaces concatenation (+=) with StringBuilder, ValueStringBuilder, or string.Create

Tests.Name: System.Text.Json: Source Generator for NativeAOT
Tests.Prompt:
Analyze this serialization code in a NativeAOT application:

var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(user);

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS:
1. Explain the runtime reflection problem with JsonSerializer without a Source Generator in NativeAOT.
2. Implement '[JsonSerializable(typeof(User))]' with a generated partial 'JsonSerializerContext'.

Criteria.Description: Explains that NativeAOT strips reflection metadata, causing JsonSerializer to fail without a Source Generator
Declares [JsonSerializable] and inherits from JsonSerializerContext correctly

var users = await JsonSerializer.DeserializeAsync<List<User>>(stream);

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS:

Tests.Name: I/O Performance: Synchronous Blocking Network and HTTP Calls

Criteria.Description: Explains that synchronous network calls (client.Send / ReadToEnd) freeze execution threads during network I/O latency
Refactors network calls using client.SendAsync / GetAsync and ReadToEndAsync / ReadAsStringAsync with await end-to-end

Tests.Name: I/O Performance: Synchronous File System Operations in Async Methods
